svg.text: FORMAT LINEAGE: Pascal Biese (LLM Watch) & Elvis Saravia (DAIR.AI) digest format
Paper of the Day: HarnessEvolve — Learning From Reference Trajectories for Reliable Agent Self-Evolution
One paper, one chart, three bullets, a verdict. Format borrowed from the daily paper-digest creators; numbers taken from Tables 1-3 of arXiv:2609.00829.
HarnessEvolve: Learning from Reference Trajectories for
Wen Jiang et al. (Sep 2026) • 5 benchmarks (SearchQA, OfficeQA, SpreadsheetBench, CloudCoreNetwork-QA, Wireless-QA)
Compare failed trajectories against clean reference trajectories for step-level credit
assignment, cluster failures into reusable skills, and enforce a two-tier competence gate.
Teams fix agent failures by hand-editing prompts after each bug, which bloats instructions,
overfits one-off cases, and silently breaks workflows that used to pass.
Reference-trajectory step-level credit assignment → failure clustering into generalizable skill
updates → two-tier competence gating (quality/leakage check + snapshot pool regression check).
CloudCoreNetwork-QA jumps from 43.4% to 86.9% (+21.6 pts over GEPA 65.3%); SpreadsheetBench
jumps from 44.3% to 76.4%; transfers across Hermes, OpenCode, LAMAgent, and DeepSeek Harness.
It turns 'prompt whack-a-mole' into a gated engineering loop: candidate updates that fail the two-tier
gate are rejected before they can regress previously solved workflows.
Requires reference trajectories and step-level trace logging; a substantial fraction of candidate
updates are rejected by the two-tier gate (which is why evaluation cost must be budgeted).
THE ONE CHART (RECREATED FROM THE PAPER'S REPORTED NUMBERS)
Reported accuracy (%) from Tables 1 & 2 of arXiv:2609.00829 comparing Base vs. strongest baseline (GEPA/ACE/SkillOpt) vs. HarnessEvolve.
METHOD IN FIVE BOXES (FOLLOW THE PACKET)
Cross-framework transfer (Table 3): skills evolved on OpenClaw transfer directly to Hermes, OpenCode
1. Export your last 20 failed traces with step indexes.
2. Diff one against a clean reference trajectory.
3. Gate every prompt/skill edit on a golden replay suite.
Verdict: READ NOW if you edit system prompts or agent skills more than once a week.
A paper is worth your time when it changes a habit; this one replaces manual prompt edits with a two-tier regression-gated loop.
Curated by Nitin Aggarwal • Google Cloud ADK + OpenHands Factory • Proprietary + Confidential
